pr_title: Fields API to allow fetching values when _source is disabled
pr_body:
Back when we introduced the fields parameter to the search API, it could only fetch values from _source, hence
the corresponding sub-fetch phase fails early whenever _source is disabled. Today though runtime fields can
be retrieved from a separate value fetcher that reads from fielddata, and metadata fields can be retrieved
from stored fields. These two scenarios currently throw an unnecessary error whenever _source is disabled.

This commit removes the check for disabled _source, so that runtime fields and metadata fields can be retrieved even when _source is disabled. Fields that need to be loaded from _source are simply skipped whenever _source is disabled, similar to when a field is not found in _source.

Closes #87072
pr_comments: Hi @javanna, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

> Feels a lot like the work I started on in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/85348 and https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/85185 but that stalled out. I'm happy to see this in though.

Yes, I did verify that you also had a similar fix in your PRs. It feels good that this goes in separately, and I will revive discussions on fetching from doc_values and possibly from stored fields too.

> I'm not sure how helpful this check is in practice

I think I agree. It would be better to return what we can retrieve instead of failing the whole request, yet silently failing to fetch does not sound like a good idea either, or should we consider doing that?

Right, I was suggesting that we remove the check altogether. I think it's already documented that if you don't have `_source` enabled (on non-runtime fields) then the fields will be missing from the response. I can see arguments both ways, but to me this approach feels the simplest and most flexible.
@jtibshirani I removed the check for _source disabled, and fixed failing tests here and there. Could you have another look please?

issue_context.title: Runtime fields and _source disabled
comments: This is definitely a bug, we should have adapted the code back when we added support for fetching runtime fields, as they can totally be retrieved with _source disabled. Looks like we did not have tests that covered this scenario.

review_comments: Moving this check is a small fix, but I think that we should revise ValueFetcher#fetchDocumentField replacing its SourceLookup argument with something else that is less specific to fetching source. It is currently misused by the fetchers that don't load from _source, it seems. happy to work on that as a follow-up, but I wanted to check if that has this been discussed before.
Yeah, it misuses it. I'm mostly ok with it because all they really want is the doc id. But there is a lot of baggage here. A cleaner interface could be much nicer.
It'd be great to clean up this interface a bit. I don't think we had concrete ideas, would be happy to discuss in a follow-up.

Could you explain the motivation for these checks `context.isSourceEnabled()`? Is it a small optimization to avoid extra work?

I saw that `FieldFetcherTests#testFetchFromSourceWithSourceDisabled` can fail without this check, but it seems like the test logic just needs to be adapted to not pass a null or empty `SourceLookup`?

yes the check helps the new test work without providing a source lookup, but mostly I was annoyed that we do extra work when we can avoid it: why call sourcePath and iterate over what it returns when we already know that we have no _source?> And why even require a non-null SourceLookup in that case? Also, the way the test is currently setup, if I provide a non null _source, fields are going to be retrieved from it no matter whether source is disabled or not, because source is not retrieved from the index but rather provided manually to the fetch method.

I guess I took a shortcut to avoid having to deal with all of the above in this PR but I'd expect things to change once SearchLookup is no longer the only required argument. With this in mind this change did not feel so bad after all.
Okay, that works for me. Maybe we'll end up revising this when we clean up the method signature.
++ thanks I will keep this in mind
